goal: Decide if a coded matrix request is computed, or which error it gets. The checks run in the order the LexLean Matmul protocol sets.

app.name: matmul-coded-admission
app.title: Coded matmul admission
app.purpose: Decide whether a coded matrix product request is computed, or answered with the protocol error the LexLean Matmul source returns first.

fields.name: version
fields.means: the protocol version that leads the request

fields.name: m
fields.means: rows of A and of the result

fields.name: k
fields.means: columns of A and stored rows of B

fields.name: n
fields.means: columns of B and of the result

fields.name: shape
fields.means: whether A has m*k entries and B-codes has k*n codes

fields.name: tier
fields.means: the scalar codec tier named after the operation

fields.name: code
fields.means: the largest stored code in B-codes

meanings.ok: the codes are decoded and the exact product is returned as 1 ok rows columns cells
meanings.unsupported-version: the request does not begin with version 1 and nothing is computed
meanings.invalid-dimension: a dimension is above the modeled maximum of 8 and nothing is allocated
meanings.shape-mismatch: A or B-codes does not have the entry count its dimensions declare
meanings.unknown-tier: the tier is not binary, ternary, signed8 or full8
meanings.invalid-code: a stored code is outside the range its tier decodes

rules.why: PROTOCOL.md and src/Protocol.lex.tex: every request begins with 1; any other version is ProtocolError.UnsupportedVersion
src/Model.lex.tex maximumDimension is 8; Protocol.lex.tex answers InvalidDimension before parsing matrices
src/Model.lex.tex maximumDimension is 8 for k as for m and n
src/Model.lex.tex maximumDimension is 8 for n as for m and k
src/Protocol.lex.tex compares a.length with m*k and b.length with k*n before the tier is read
src/Protocol.lex.tex validTier accepts exactly binary, ternary, signed8 and full8
src/Core.lex.tex validCode: binary codes 0,1 decode to -1,+1
src/Core.lex.tex validCode: ternary codes 0,1,2 decode to -1,0,+1
src/Core.lex.tex validCode: signed8 codes are bytes 0..255 read as two complement
src/Core.lex.tex validCode: full8 codes are bytes 0..255

app.otherwiseWhy: version 1, every dimension at most 8, conformant shapes, a known tier and in-range codes: decode the code, accumulate exactly, encode once

properties.why: ERRORS.md: InvalidDimension has seven negative vectors; no product is computed above the dimension bound
src/Core.lex.tex: a binary code above 1 is never decoded
the version is checked before any other field
an unknown tier is reported as such, never as an invalid code

stakeholders.name: Numerical researcher
stakeholders.text: Runs coded and quantized products in the workbench and needs every rejected request to name the error the source declares.

stakeholders.name: Integrator
stakeholders.text: Calls the generated native library or Core-Wasm guest and needs out-of-range dimensions and codes refused before any allocation.

concerns.name: Bounded allocation
concerns.text: No request with a dimension above 8 or an undecodable code reaches matrix allocation or decoding.

components.name: LexLean Matmul workbench
components.text: The research workbench on GitHub Pages that sends version 1 protocol requests from a browser worker.

components.name: Independent arithmetic oracles
components.text: The reference UOR matmul oracles the just vv gate replays native and Wasm results against.

threats.name: Oversized dimension
threats.text: A request declares a dimension above 8 to force a large allocation in the guest.

control.name: Dimension bound first
control.text: Dimensions are checked against maximumDimension before matrices are parsed or allocated.

threats.name: Out-of-book code
threats.text: A stored code outside its tier is decoded into a value the tier does not define, changing the product.

control.name: Tier code range
control.text: Each tier admits only the codes validCode accepts, and a binary code above 1 is never computed.

threats.name: Misreported shape
threats.text: A caller reports a conformant shape for matrices whose entry counts do not match.
threats.accepted: The app decides from the shape it is given; counting entries belongs to the protocol parser in src/Protocol.lex.tex, whose ten shape-mismatch vectors cover it.

quality.text: Each of the five protocol errors the coded operation can return is the answer to some request.
quality.measureText: Outcomes of the spec that no request answers.

quality.text: A request with an out-of-range dimension or code is never computed.
quality.measureText: Requests above the dimension bound or out of code range that answer ok.
